NS-1 (i) fails: the timeline records driver_pressed_here_at as null — the driver never tapped "I'm Here", which he himself admits in his statement.

The driver's claim that he was physically present ('I was there') cannot save the fee, because NS-1 requires the app button to have been pressed, not merely physical presence; the GPS showing 5 min 20 s within 200 m (F2) satisfies only condition (ii), never (i).
Because at least one of NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) is not fulfilled, the rider is not liable for the $6.61 and it must be refunded in full.

The fee is therefore a disputed cancellation fee under NS-0 with cancelled_by = driver and a no-show claim, and the rider filed this dispute on the day of the trip, well inside the 30-day window, so relief is available (as a Ryde voucher).
The rider's own record is clean — 2.0-year account, rating 4.5, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days — which is consistent with her account that she was on her way down and not a genuine no-show.

weaknesses: The system records do show the driver genuinely waited at the pickup point: he was within 200 m from 22:39:45 with 5 min 20 s cumulative inside 200 m (F2), approached to 33 m (F1) and stood stationary 38 m away for 4 minutes (F3), and texted from the pickup point (F9). The other side will argue this is a real, good-faith wait and that denying the fee is a technicality. NS-1 does not allow that argument: condition (i) is a hard requirement and F6 shows it was never met.

Rider-side facts are thin on her own conduct: there is no fact showing how far away she was or when she would have arrived, and she did not reply to the driver's 22:44 message (F10). events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.95)
events.body:
The rider disputes a $6.61 cancellation fee after the driver cancelled the trip [F4][F7]. Because the cancellation was made by the driver on a no-show claim, NS-0 routes the dispute exclusively through NS-1/NS-2 [F4][NS-0].

NS-1 makes the $6.61 fee conditional on three cumulative requirements. Condition (i) is that the driver pressed "I'm Here" or the platform auto-confirmed arrival. The timeline shows driver_pressed_here_at is null, i.e. the button was never pressed [F6], and the driver's own statement confirms he "forgot to press the I'm Here button" [F11][NS-1].

Conditions (ii) and (iii) are in fact satisfied on the system records: the driver was first within 200 m at 22:39:45 with 5 min 20 s cumulative inside the radius and a closest approach of 33 m [F1][F2], and he stood stationary 38 m from the pickup for 4 min 0 s before cancelling [F3][NS-1]. But a satisfied (ii) and (iii) cannot substitute for the missing (i); NS-1 requires all three.

Because NS-1 (i) fails, NS-2 applies: the fee is refunded in full [F6][NS-2]. The refund figure is the cancellation fee on record, $6.61, with surge 1.0× and no other chargeable item [F7][F8][NS-2]. This is an administrative correction rather than a penalty finding; the anti-fraud flag in NS-2 is NOT triggered because the driver's GPS position was inside the pickup range throughout and there was no contradictory "I'm Here" tap to flag [F1][F2][F6][NS-2]. The dispute was filed within the 30-day window, so the relief is payable as a Ryde voucher [F4][NS-7].

claims.assertion: The $6.61 cancellation fee was charged because the driver cancelled as a no-show, so the fee's validity is governed solely by NS-1's three cumulative conditions.
NS-1 (i) fails: the timeline records driver_pressed_here_at as null — the driver never tapped "I'm Here", which he himself admits in his statement.

The driver's claim that he was physically present ('I was there') cannot save the fee, because NS-1 requires the app button to have been pressed, not merely physical presence; the GPS showing 5 min 20 s within 200 m (F2) satisfies only condition (ii), never (i).
Because at least one of NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) is not fulfilled, the rider is not liable for the $6.61 and it must be refunded in full.

The fee is therefore a disputed cancellation fee under NS-0 with cancelled_by = driver and a no-show claim, and the rider filed this dispute on the day of the trip, well inside the 30-day window, so relief is available (as a Ryde voucher).
The rider's own record is clean — 2.0-year account, rating 4.5, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days — which is consistent with her account that she was on her way down and not a genuine no-show.

weaknesses: The system records do show the driver genuinely waited at the pickup point: he was within 200 m from 22:39:45 with 5 min 20 s cumulative inside 200 m (F2), approached to 33 m (F1) and stood stationary 38 m away for 4 minutes (F3), and texted from the pickup point (F9). The other side will argue this is a real, good-faith wait and that denying the fee is a technicality. NS-1 does not allow that argument: condition (i) is a hard requirement and F6 shows it was never met.

Rider-side facts are thin on her own conduct: there is no fact showing how far away she was or when she would have arrived, and she did not reply to the driver's 22:44 message (F10). The driver can argue the wait exceeded three minutes (F3) and that nothing in the record shows she was descending. NS-2 turns only on the unmet (i) condition, not on whether she was actually en route.

No account flag is available here: the driver has a clean record (F16: 1059-day account, 4.69 rating, 770 trips, 0 disputes/0 upheld in 90 days), and RC-6/NS-2 repeat-offender conditions are not met, so I do not ask for flag_account — only the fee refund.

claims.assertion: The GPS record shows the driver reached the pickup: closest approach 33 m at 22:41:00, first within 200 m at 22:39:45, and 5 min 20 s cumulatively within 200 m before cancellation — i.e. the driver was indisputably at the pickup point in the sense of NS-1(ii).
The driver was stationary 38 m from the pickup for a continuous 4 min 0 s (22:41:05–22:45:05), exceeding the >3 minute waiting requirement in NS-1(iii).

The driver really did wait and then cancelled believing the rider a no-show: at 22:41 he messaged 'At the pickup point, black Hyundai Ioniq' and at 22:44 'Waited 4 min, cancelling' — conduct consistent with the stationary GPS record and offered for context, not as the basis of the finding.

The single missing NS-1 element is the 'I'm Here' tap: the timeline shows driver_pressed_here_at is null, so requirement NS-1(i) is not met and NS-2 therefore directs a full refund of the $6.61 cancellation fee rather than a driver payout.

The NS-2 account flag for tapping 'I'm Here' while off-location does not apply here, because the driver never tapped the button at all (F6) and his GPS position was inside the pickup range throughout (F1, F2) — the anti-fraud trigger requires a contradictory tap-plus-location record.

No aggravating factor supports any account action against the driver: profile shows 770 trips in 90 days, rating 4.69, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in the last 90 days, so the 'repeated abuse' premise of a flag is absent.

The rider's own account is clean (719 days, 4.5 rating, no disputes in 90 days), so the $6.61 is best resolved by refunding it to the rider as an administrative correction rather than by any punishment finding against the driver.

Refund amount is computable and non-discretionary: the cancellation fee on record is $6.61 (surge multiplier 1.0×, no other fees), so the full-refund figure under NS-2 is exactly $6.61, issued as a Ryde voucher within the 30-day post-trip window.

weaknesses: The decisive requirement is against us: F6 shows driver_pressed_here_at is null, so NS-1(i) fails and NS-2 mandates a full $6.61 refund — the driver cannot be paid the $4.50 share however long he actually waited.

The rider's complaint 'I was on my way down' is not contradicted by any system record showing she was told not to come or that she refused the wait; the GPS facts (F2, F3) prove the driver was present but do not prove the rider was absent at the door, so the rider will argue the cancellation was premature.

The driver's written statement (F11) is a self-serving statement that conflicts with the timeline on the 'I'm Here' step; under the system-records-win rule the rider will use F6 and F11 together to portray the driver as having skipped the required procedural step.

Surrounding traffic (F12, F13, F14) offers no excuse for the cancellation — Woodlands Avenue 5 at speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) is below the RD-4(b) band 1–2 threshold and no incident was recorded (F13), so the driver has no 'reasonable cause' narrative for ending the trip.

points.response: Accepted as far as it goes: F1 (33 m closest approach), F2 (5 min 20 s within 200 m) and F5 (arrival recorded 22:39:45) do establish NS-1 condition (ii). But (ii) is only one of three cumulative requirements, and it cannot carry the fee on its own.

Accepted: F3 shows 4 min 0 s stationary 38 m from the pickup, so NS-1 condition (iii) is met. It is still irrelevant to the outcome, because a satisfied (ii) plus (iii) with an unmet (i) is exactly the NS-2 fact pattern.

The driver's chat (F9, F10) and statement (F11) are user-submitted content and lose to the timeline: F6 records driver_pressed_here_at as null, so the messages show intent to wait, not compliance with NS-1(i); the stationary GPS in F3 supports their version of where he stood but not the procedural step he skipped.
No dispute on liability: this is the driver's own concession that NS-1(i) fails and NS-2 directs a full refund of the $6.61 charged (F7 on record, F4 cancellation by driver).

Accepted, and the rider does not seek any account flag: NS-2's flag attaches only to an 'I'm Here' tap contradicted by GPS, and F6 shows no tap at all, so the anti-fraud trigger is absent. I therefore ask only for the fee refund, not flag_account.
Accepted: F16 (770 trips, 4.69 rating, 0 disputes/0 upheld in 90 days) means the 'repeated' premise for any account action is missing, and my brief never requested one.

Agreed on the result but not the framing: this is not discretionary goodwill, it is NS-2's mandatory consequence of an unmet NS-1(i) (F6), refundable as a voucher under NS-7 — the rider's clean record (F15) only corroborates that she was descending and was not a genuine no-show.
Accepted: the refund is exactly $6.61, taken from the cancellation fee on record in F7 with surge 1.0× (F8) and no other chargeable item, issued as a Ryde voucher per NS-7.
Accepted: with cancelled_by = driver plus a no-show claim, NS-0 routes this dispute into NS-1/NS-2, and that is the framework I have applied in D1–D4.
Conceded on the fact and on its effect: F6 records driver_pressed_here_at as null, and the driver admits it in F11, so NS-1(i) is not satisfied and the fee cannot stand.

Accepted — I never built the driver's case on presence alone: D1/D2 use F1, F2 and F3 only to prove the wait was genuine (NS-1(ii)(iii)), and D4 accepts NS-1(i) fails on F6, which is exactly why the remedy is the NS-2 refund rather than any payment to the driver.

Agreed in full and already in my own brief at D4/D8: because NS-1(i) fails on F6, NS-2 requires the full $6.61 to be refunded to the rider, and F7 confirms that is the exact amount charged (surge 1.0×).

Not contested on the timebar: the trip and dispute sit within the 30-day window, so the $6.61 relief is payable as a Ryde voucher under NS-7 — my difference with the rider side is purely that NS-2 also does not expose the driver to any account action here.

The rider's clean profile (F15) does not bear on NS-1: her account standing cannot supply the missing 'I'm Here' tap from F6, and equally the driver's record (F16: 0 disputes, 0 upheld) shows no abuse pattern, so NS-2's flag is not triggered on either side.
